q: A hospital must keep patient text inside its own cloud account with private networking and audit logs, and wants a frontier-class model. Best first choice?
options: Managed cloud platform in their account with private connectivity
Direct provider API with an API key in env vars
why: A managed platform inside the existing cloud account fits network, audit and contract needs. The direct API fails the boundary requirement; laptops cannot meet operations or scale.

q: Traffic is a steady 24/7 high volume of simple classification. Which cost shape likely wins?
options: Self-hosted small open model on well-utilized GPUs
Provisioned capacity for the biggest model
why: High steady utilization amortizes GPU cost and a small model suffices. Per-token frontier models cost more at that volume.

q: Which statement about open weights is most accurate?
options: They are always open source with no restrictions
They can be consumed per token without running GPUs, but licenses and host quantization matter
They always beat closed models on quality
why: Hosted per-token access exists, yet license terms and host serving choices change what you actually get.

q: When does adding a gateway in front of a single platform make sense?
options: When you need multi-team budgets, multiple providers or failover
why: A gateway earns its place with concrete governance or failover needs; it adds a hop and can hide features.

q: Which question applies equally to every managed AI platform?
options: Which models are available in my region with my access and quota?
How many logos on the pricing page?
Which SDK language did marketing pick?
why: Region, access and quota decide usability on every platform. The others are irrelevant.

q: You build on a catalog alias that points to 'latest' version. What is the main risk?
options: Behavior can change without a code change
why: Aliases can move to a new version with different outputs. Pin exact ids and re-evaluate on change.

q: Which is NOT something the platform generally provides?
options: Evidence that your answers are correct for your task
why: Correctness evaluation for your application is your responsibility; the platform supplies infrastructure.

q: Swapping to another model in the same catalog broke JSON output downstream. Best fix?
options: Add schema validation and include structured-output tests in the eval before swapping
why: Models differ in schema adherence; evaluate and validate. Retrying only masks the issue.

q: Why is a role with short-lived credentials better than a static key?
options: Nothing long-lived to leak, automatic rotation and per-workload attribution
It removes the need for logging
why: Short-lived ambient credentials reduce leak impact and give attribution. Speed and outputs are unaffected.

q: An app role has permission to invoke any model. What is the main risk?
options: A bug or compromise can use costly or unapproved models
why: Wildcards widen blast radius in cost and data exposure. Scope to approved ids.

q: Two customers share a vector index without tenant filtering. What is likely?
why: Without tenant filters, retrieval can surface another tenant's data, a data leak.

q: What does a customer-managed key NOT protect?
options: Ability to disable access via key revocation
Data while being processed in the service's memory
why: CMK covers data at rest and gives key control; it does not guarantee processing-time confidentiality.

q: Which is a valid reason a working dev setup fails in prod region?
options: Model access or quota not granted there
why: Availability and quotas are per region and account.

q: Calls stay in-region, yet an audit finds data abroad. Most plausible source?
options: A third-party observability or embedding service in another region
why: Side components often leave the boundary; map the full data flow.

q: What is the best way to know a provider does not train on your data?
options: Written contractual or official terms for the product, dated and recorded
why: Terms differ by product; written, dated evidence belongs in the vendor review.

q: Required model absent in-region and data must stay in country. Best path?
options: Evaluate an in-region comparable model or self-host an open model in region
why: Staying in boundary requires an in-region alternative; silent cross-border routing breaches policy.

q: Traffic has a flat daily baseline plus occasional spikes. Best capacity strategy?
options: Provision the baseline and serve spikes on-demand
why: Reserve the steady portion where utilization justifies it; spikes are cheaper on-demand.

q: Throttling occurs though real tokens are low. Which cause fits best?
options: A very large max-output setting counted against quota
why: Some platforms count requested max tokens at admission, burning quota.

q: After throttling, all clients retry immediately. What happens?
why: Synchronized retries multiply load; use backoff, jitter and retry budgets.

q: Average cost per request is on target but spend is 3x. First thing to inspect?
why: Long-tail or looping requests dominate bills; examine p95 and per-task cost.

q: Why prefer cost per successful task over cost per call?
options: Retries, loops and failures hide real cost
why: A cheap model needing retries or multiple calls can cost more per outcome.

q: Which best prevents an overnight agent loop from draining budget?
options: Iteration and token caps plus spend-rate alerts and a kill switch
why: Preventive hard limits and real-time alerts stop it; invoice review is after the fact.

q: A checkpoint ships as a pickle file from an unknown uploader. Main risk?
why: Pickle deserialization can run code; prefer safetensors and vetted sources.

q: Same open model, two providers, different outputs. Most likely reason?
why: Serving configuration differences change outputs; evaluate each endpoint.

q: A 20%-utilized dedicated GPU costs how much per useful token versus fully utilized (illustrative)?
why: Fixed hourly cost spread over fewer tokens; 20% utilization means about 5x.

q: A 7B model at 16-bit needs roughly what for weights (illustrative)?
why: 2 bytes per parameter times 7B is about 14 GB, before KV cache.

q: Interactive chatbot, scale-to-zero, 60+ s first replies. Best change?
options: Keep a minimum warm replica during user hours
why: Cold start loads weights; warm replicas remove it from the user path.

q: Which is a fair way to compare open and closed models?
options: Prompts tuned for the closed model only
Your own eval set with tuned prompts per model plus cost per successful task
why: Own data, fair prompting and cost per outcome give a valid decision.

q: A gateway fails over to a different model on timeout. What is the biggest hidden risk?
options: The fallback may behave differently in format, safety or quality
why: Failover changes who answers; fallbacks must be evaluated for the task and logged.

q: Which error type should NOT trigger fail over?
why: A malformed request fails on every backend; retrying elsewhere just wastes calls.

q: Why prefer virtual keys over sharing provider keys?
options: They remove the need for logs
Per-team budgets, attribution and revocation without rotating provider keys
why: Virtual keys give governance and limit blast radius.

q: The semantic cache returns another tenant's answer. Primary fix?
options: Include tenant and permission scope in cache keys
why: Tenant isolation must be part of the key.

q: A one-team, one-provider app with stable needs. Best choice?
options: Thin in-code wrapper, add gateway when needs appear
why: A gateway adds critical-path complexity not yet justified.

q: Compliance bars third-party data transit but you want unified routing. Which is best?
why: Self-hosting keeps data in your boundary while giving routing features.

q: What does a gateway standardize?
options: Transport and API shape, not behavior
why: Behavior still differs by model; evaluation is needed.

q: Managed knowledge base misses table data. First step?
options: Check parsing and chunking settings and measure retrieval recall on a test set
why: Retrieval, not generation, is the likely fault; measure recall.

q: Which is the most portable asset in a managed evaluation setup?
options: Your labeled golden set and rubrics
why: Datasets and rubrics let you re-run anywhere.

q: Managed fine-tuned model cannot be exported. Main implication?
options: Lock-in and re-tuning when the base is deprecated
why: Keep training data and recipe so you can retrain elsewhere.

q: Guardrails block legitimate questions. Best action?
options: Measure false positives on labeled data and tune policies
why: Tune on evidence; do not remove protections blindly.

q: Which layers are usually worth owning?
options: Evaluation data, prompts and domain tools
why: Those define product quality and are your differentiators.

q: A cheap managed option has a 6-month exit cost. How should this enter the decision?
options: Count it as priced lock-in and compare with benefits
Only consider it if the price is zero
why: Exit cost is part of total cost and risk.

q: Team is small, use case standard, platform already compliant. Best?
options: Buy managed building blocks with documented revisit triggers
why: Buying non-differentiating layers is honest; track triggers.

q: Which item is least likely to travel to a new platform?
why: Platform-specific configs must be rebuilt.

q: Why is migration mostly evaluation work?
options: Behavior differences in quality, format, tools and safety must be measured
why: The code change is small; behavior risk dominates.

q: Which cutover pattern has no user impact while collecting comparison data?
why: Shadow copies traffic without serving the results.

q: A pinned model version is announced for retirement. What should exist?
options: An eval suite ready to qualify a replacement and a scheduled migration
why: Qualifying replacements needs a ready eval and planned time.

q: Best framing of lock-in?
options: Known, priced and accepted, with isolation behind interfaces
why: Zero lock-in is costly; manage it deliberately.

q: A team wants multi-cloud without a driver. Cheaper alternative?
options: Single primary cloud, abstraction, tested exit and model-call fallback
why: Gets most resilience benefits at lower complexity.

q: A prototype used a public API on synthetic tickets. Production will see real claims text in India. What stays and what must change?
options: Keep the API key and add PII redaction
Keep the prompt and evals; move invoke to an in-region managed platform with IAM
Retrain a 70B model from scratch in-country
Switch to a consumer chat app with SSO
why: The prompt and golden set travel. Claims text cannot leave on a public key. An in-region platform with cloud identity is the least-ops path that clears the boundary.

q: After a quarter on Bedrock, which artefact is usually the most expensive to leave behind?
options: A managed knowledge-base index and its IAM/network wiring
The application interface behind a complete() wrapper
why: Prompts, evals and a thin interface travel. Proprietary indexes and account wiring are rebuilds. That is the switching cost after month one.

q: You need a vendor-only citation field the unified Converse-style API drops. Honest move?
options: Forge the field in the gateway
Call native passthrough on that one route and list it as accepted lock-in
why: Unified APIs hide some features. An isolated escape hatch keeps the rest portable. Forging or ignoring citations is worse than a named lock-in.

q: A catalog alias pointed at latest moved quality overnight with no deploy. First fix?
options: Pin the previous snapshot id and compare on the frozen eval
why: Floating aliases are silent model swaps. Pin the last known id, re-score, then schedule a real replacement eval.

q: A nightly eval job reused the production app role and can invoke every chat model. What should change?
options: Add the public API key as backup
Bind the job to a workload identity that can invoke only the two named eval model ids
Run the job as a human SSO user
why: Least privilege is a different role per worker. Reusing the app role lets a confused batch escalate the bill and the blast radius.

q: The private endpoint is down. A teammate adds a NAT so calls can reach the public model URL. Why is that usually wrong?
options: Public fallback is required by every platform
It re-opens public egress that policy forbade unless a written exception exists
why: Private connectivity's value is the closed path. An undocumented public fallback is a policy breach, not a mitigation.

q: Inference is in ap-south-1 but traces sit in a US eval SaaS. What failed?
options: Nothing if GPUs are in India
Only the embedding model region matters
Prompt and log residency — copies of prompts are still processing
why: Residency covers prompts, completions and traces, not only where the GPU sat. A US log store fails an in-country rule.

q: What is acceptable evidence that prompts are not used to train?
options: A verbal assurance on a sales call
The contract clause plus the console or API setting, dated
why: Training-opt-out is a written clause and a setting you can show. Marketing pages and defaults are not controls.

q: A summariser of 40-page PDFs 429s while RPM is at 10%. Which quota did you hit?
why: Long-context jobs burn TPM first. Raising RPM will not help. Read both graphs in the production region.

q: Spend doubled overnight. Which first-three playbook is right?
options: Buy a larger reserved unit, then look at traces
Check agent/tool loops, cache-hit cliff, and whether an alias floated to a pricier id
why: Loops, cache misses and silent model swaps are the usual culprits. Reserving more capacity before diagnosis hides the fire.

q: An 8B model in 16-bit is ~16GB of weights but a 24GB card OOMs at 8k context batch 8. Likely cause?
options: KV-cache growth with layers, heads, context and batch
The eval set is too small
why: Serving memory is weights plus KV-cache. Parameter count alone under-sizes long context and batch.

q: You want to ship 4-bit because a blog showed good perplexity. What do you do instead?
options: Measure 8-bit and 4-bit on your held-out set and schema probe
why: Quantisation quality is task-specific. A blog number is not your eval. Re-score the artefact you will serve.

q: Failover from model A to model B silently drops tools and the user still gets fluent text. What should the gateway have done?
options: Strip tools only as a marked degraded path, or skip B for tool requests
why: A backup that cannot take the schema is not a fallback for that request. Silent strip is worse than an error because it looks healthy.

q: When does a router earn the extra hop?
options: Always, on day one with one provider
When you have several providers or teams or spend worth governing — not for one key
why: A gateway is a critical-path hop. One team and one provider can use a client library until a second provider or chargeback need appears.

q: A managed guardrail blocks 11% of allowed clinical FAQs. First move?
options: Measure against a signed false-positive budget and tune or queue the slice
why: Over-block is a measured rate. Tune categories or add a human queue. Disabling the filter throws away the must-block side.

q: Which four rows belong on a one-page build-versus-buy scorecard for an AI add-on?
options: Logo count, blog rank, employee count, colour
Control, eval depth, cost at 10× volume, auditor explainability
why: Those four flip the decision. Suite checkboxes and logos do not. 10× is where SKU cliffs appear.

q: Shadow traffic to a new platform must still be approved for the data class. Why?
options: Copies are still processing even if users never see the new output
why: A mirrored prompt is a copy in another processor. Unapproved shadow of regulated text is a breach.

q: A catalog version is retired in 30 days and the only owner is on leave. What should already exist?
options: A deputy, a warm candidate, and a runbook the deputy can execute
A handwritten model card with no eval
why: A deprecation runbook names owner, deputy, eval gate and fallback. Heroics on day 28 are the failure.
